To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CSF1 expression in spinal cord is increased in experimental autoimmune encephalyomyelitis (a mouse model of multiple sclerosis).
CSF1 expression is increased in the mouse spinal cord during EAE and CSF1 up‐regulation may contribute to microglial proliferation/activation, demyelination, and neuronal loss in EAE.

CSF1 is expressed in spinal motoneurons and its upregulation in EAE correlates with microglia activation and neuronal loss, and over‐expression of spinal CSF1 induces microglia proliferation, activation and neuronal loss in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CSF1 on the proliferation and activation microglia and its potential contribution to the neuronal loss in EAE.
the role of CSF1 up-regulation in CNS in EAE.
the role of CSF1 on microglia activation and neurodegeneration in EAE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CSF1 is a crucial factor that regulates the proliferation and activation status of microglia, which in turn contributes to neuronal death in the spinal cord with EAE.
CSF1 plays a crucial role in microglial proliferation, activation and neurodegeneration, especially in the motoneuron loss in EAE.
CSF1 is a key factor in the development of neurodegeneration and demyelination in EAE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CSF1 is an important regulator of microglia proliferation and activation in EAE and CSF1‐mediated neuroinflammation may contribute to the pathogenesis of MS and other neurodegenerative diseases.
microglial proliferation is a major cause for the neuroinflammation in EAE.
CSF1 is upregulated in the CNS with EAE and CSF1 expression in neurons is associated with microglial proliferation, activation, and neuronal loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microglia may play an important and active role in neuronal degeneration and demyelination in multiple sclerosis and other neuroinflammatory diseases.
CSF1 is a potential target in the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.
CSF1 is upregulated in the mouse spinal cord with EAE and the upregulation of CSF1 may play a critical role in microglial proliferation, activation, and neuronal loss.
